Monitoring: Mealybugs are tiny, less than 0.5 cm wingless insects.
They are soft- bodied and covered by white wax.
Note that whiteflies are also white and small, but will fly off when shaking the plant.
Mealybugs are found around stems and leaf nodes.
They do not move or only slowly move.
Examine field for white non-moving mealy bugs at least once per week.
Consider control when about 5 to 10 mealybugs have been found on 4-10 plants per quarter of an acre
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Spray fermented, diluted cow urine as it irritates the soft body of the insect

Put urine or urine/manure mixture in a hole of about 45cm 3 ; add soil of about half a spade; leave it to ferment for 10-14 days; dilute with water at ratios of 1:2 -1:6; add soap of 0.5-1g per 10 to 20L of solution.
Test the diluted cow urine on one or two plants to ensure a safe concentration.
Restricted re-entry interval - once spray is dry, entry is permitted.

Direct Control (Chemical): Spraying of pesticides on cassava plant is not advisable as these will kill natural enemies of the cassava pests.
Moreover, cassava leaves are consumed and should not be covered with pesticides.

When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (MAFC / TPRI).
